summary: Not a compiler defect: asks what the project publishes as release artifacts, so no compile can answer it. Still true - 0 macOS assets across all 26 published tagged releases (73 assets enumerated), while Linux shipped from v1.7.2212 onward. One unpublished draft had zero assets at capture time; querying its empty tag with gh release view would silently return the latest published release and double-count its three assets. The gap is publication, not the build: azure-pipelines.yml is configured to build and run check-all on macOS on every PR (MacOS_Clang_Release/Debug), and macOS has been a CI configuration since the 2018 Travis bots, but the Nix job publishes only test results. The DXIL-signing blocker cited in the thread no longer applies - lib/DxilHash and dxildll are in-tree and not WIN32-gated, 6770 closed (source-level evidence only; nothing was built or run on macOS). The stated blocker is now Apple code signing, and a maintainer has said there are no plans. What remains is a policy decision, not a measurement.
title: Binary release artifacts for macOS
